questions.q: What does the Snowflake Kafka Sink Connector actually do, according to this lesson?
options: Lands a topic's events as rows in a Snowflake table, config-driven, with Snowpipe Streaming buffering underneath
Runs custom Spark transform code before writing to Snowflake
Replaces the need for a Kafka topic entirely
Only works with Databricks, not Snowflake
questions.explain: It's a Kafka Connect sink connector configured with connection details — no custom transform code runs on this path.

questions.q: How does Databricks' spark.readStream.format("kafka") relate to what Structured Streaming Basics (Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 33) already taught?
options: It's the same readStream API from that lesson, just pointed at Kafka as the source instead of a file source
It's a completely unrelated API that has nothing to do with Structured Streaming
It only works after the Snowflake connector has already processed the data
readStream cannot read from Kafka at all
questions.explain: Kafka is just another Structured Streaming source — swapping the format to "kafka" and pointing subscribe at the topic is the only real change from that lesson's file-based example.

questions.q: What is the real difference between the Snowflake and Databricks landing patterns for the same Kafka topic, per this lesson?
options: Snowflake's connector is config-driven with no transform logic; Databricks' readStream can run a full Spark transform before the data lands
There is no real difference — both do exactly the same thing
Snowflake's connector can run Spark code, but Databricks' readStream cannot
Only Databricks can read from a Kafka topic; Snowflake cannot
questions.explain: The Snowflake path is fast and config-only for raw rows; the Databricks path is the right call when the events need real processing before they're useful.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why might a real platform run both the Snowflake connector and Databricks' readStream off the same orders topic?
options: Kafka's replay property means multiple independent consumers can read the same topic without affecting each other, so each can serve a different downstream purpose
Kafka only allows one consumer to read a topic at a time, so this is never actually possible
Running both is required by Kafka's architecture
Snowflake and Databricks cannot both read from the same topic
questions.explain: As Lesson 1 established, a Kafka topic supports any number of independent consumers reading it at their own pace, for their own purposes.

questions.q: Where does Snowflake's own course cover what happens when a Snowpipe load like this one actually fails?
options: Lesson 20, Handling Failed Snowpipe Loads, in that course's Chapter 4 ("Snowpipe & Automated Ingestion")
Snowflake's course never covers failed loads
It's covered in the Databricks course instead
It's covered in this same Kafka lesson in full detail
questions.explain: Chapter 4 of the Snowflake course covers the full Snowpipe arc: continuous ingestion (Lesson 18), monitoring loads (Lesson 19), and handling failed loads (Lesson 20).
